newsitem.title: USA: Dana buys off-highway parts maker.
newsitem.headline: Dana buys off-highway parts maker.

text.p: Dana Corp. said Friday it has agreed to acquire Clark-Hurth Components, a maker of off-highway vehicle parts, from Ingersoll-Rand Co.
Terms were not disclosed but Dana said the acquisition was the largest in its 92-year history.

Dana said it will combine the Clark-Hurth operations with its Spicer Off-Highway divisions to form an Off-Highway Components Group that will produce axles, brakes, and powershift transmissions for vehicles used in agriculture, construction, forestry, leisure and outdoor power equipment, mining and material handling.
With 12 plants in four countries, the group will serve hundreds of off-highway equipment manufacturers in more than 30 countries, Dana said.
"This acquisition will make Dana a leading supplier of off-highway drivetrain components and systems," Dana Chairman Southwood Morcott said in the statement.
It will also strengthen Toledo, Ohio-based Dana's international presence because two-thirds of Clark-Hurth sales are outside the United States, he said.
Clark-Hurth has manufacturing plants in Belgium, Italy and the United States, and more than half of its sales totalling about $350 million in 1995 are in Europe, Dana said.
Spicer has plants in the United States, Britain and Italy. Dana said the acquisition better positions it for Asian and South American markets as well.
The deal is subject to regulatory approval, Dana said.
Dana's stock rose 75 cents to $32.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
